summary: TRACK 5: found a duplicate project card + duplicated JSON-LD ItemList links, a split GitHub identity across the site, a mismatched resume-generator email, and a wrong tour.js target — all outside verify.py's 17 checks.
result_text:
TRACK 5 — Content, credential-claim & SEO/AEO integrity
Verified against live clone, HEAD 04f3c3657c218e604c2def99a8c90a423db4947d. CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/README.md read; graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md consulted first per AGENTS.md rule before grepping source. All findings below confirmed NOT caught by verify.py's 17 checks (traced check_asset_references, check_internal_hrefs, check_sitemap_sync, check_search_index_sync source to confirm scope gaps before flagging).

BLOCKER
1. assets/js/modules/ui.js:716 — RESUME_DATA.contact (feeds the ATS Resume Generator/Exporter, v43 — the actual downloadable artifact recruiters take away) uses email "aaradhya.dev.tamrakar@gmail.com" (dotted). Every other instance sitewide — README.md, index.html JSON-LD, contact.html (link + mailto + JSON-LD), terminal.js, core.js masterEmails, about.html, privacy.html, terms.html — uses "aaradhyadevtmr@gmail.com" (no dots), 15+ occurrences. If the dotted address is unowned/dead, the one document meant to get recruiters to actually contact him has a broken email. Fix: confirm which address is real, correct ui.js:716.

HIGH
2. projects.html:699 vs :918 — #p-018 and #p-018-fuse are byte-identical duplicate cards (same "P — 018" index label, title "BiasAperture — Vision Fairness & Bias Audit", description, tags). Inflates displayed project count to 30 when unique content is 29, and the P-024 slot is silently skipped (numbering never reaches p-024) — this explains the "project count varies across tracker entries" discrepancy flagged in the parent task. Both ids also leak into assets/js/script.js's SEARCH_STATIC_INDEX (line ~556 href=projects.html#p-018, line ~619 href=projects.html#p-018-fuse), so BiasAperture appears twice in command-palette search results. Not caught by verify.py since the two ids are technically unique (check_global_id_uniqueness passes) and the static index is internally self-consistent with the duplicated DOM (check_search_index_sync passes). Fix: delete the #p-018-fuse card and its search-index entry, renumber if p-024 was meant to exist.

3. projects.html JSON-LD ItemList (script block ~line 27, @type ItemList) — this AEO-facing structured data lists only 3 of 29 projects as "position 1/2/3", and 2 of those 3 entries point to anchors that don't exist on the page:
   - position 1 "SPARK — Intelligent Elderly Fall Detection Wearable" → url ".../projects.html#spark" — no id="spark" exists anywhere in projects.html (actual card id is p-015, title "SPARK — Two-Layer Fall Detection Wearable"). Confirmed via grep: zero matches for id="spark".
   - position 3 "PulseLive — Real-Time Diagnostic Hub" → url ".../projects.html#pulselive" — no id="pulselive" exists (actual card id is p-020, title "Pulse Live — Real-Time Interactive Polling Platform" — completely different subtitle, "Diagnostic Hub" vs "Interactive Polling Platform"). Confirmed via grep: zero matches for id="pulselive".
   - position 2 "PrakopNet — Multi-Hazard Early Warning System" → url ".../projects.html#p-010" is the only one of the three that's actually correct (matches live card id p-010).
   This is NOT caught by verify.py's check_internal_hrefs, which only matches literal href="file#frag" HTML attributes via regex — it does not parse JSON-LD script content, so a fragment-URL string embedded in a JSON blob is invisible to it. Any AI/search crawler consuming this ItemList (its entire purpose) gets 2 dead anchors and one stale project name/subtitle out of 3. Fix: update urls to #p-015 and #p-020, and sync PulseLive's stated name/subtitle to match the live card.

4. GitHub identity split three ways for the same person:
   - Primary sitewide CTA: index.html JSON-LD Person.sameAs, contact.html:517, core.js:24 (nav SOCIAL_ICONS), terminal.js:120 (contact command) → all use "github.com/AaradhyaDT"
   - Actual dev/hosting account, referenced 30+ times in journey.html (every commit/workflow link) and in README.md's own Contact section ("GitHub: github.com/Aaradhya-Dev-Tamrakar"), and in ui.js:716's resume data, and in ui.js:26's release-notes commit links (correctly, since that's the real repo) → "github.com/Aaradhya-Dev-Tamrakar"
   - A third variant, "github.com/AaradhyaDTmr", appears twice in journey.html (lines ~1892-1933) pointing to a legacy predecessor repo/commit history — this one looks intentionally archival (old "Repo A" CV site), not a bug, but worth confirming it's not itself stale/renamed.
   Net effect: the "GitHub" link a visitor or crawler clicks from the nav, footer, contact page, or JSON-LD sameAs lands on a different account than the one that actually hosts every linked project repo. Fix: pick one canonical GitHub identity and make sameAs/nav/terminal/contact.html consistent with it.

5. assets/js/modules/tour.js:18 — the guided product-tour step for "Featured Build (SPARK)" targets selector '#p-001', but #p-001 is the Gesture-Controlled Self-Balancing Robot (GCSBR) card, not SPARK (which is #p-015). The tour will highlight/scroll to the wrong project card entirely. Same line also asserts "98.4% precision" for SPARK — this figure appears nowhere else in the repo (single occurrence, grepped repo-wide) and directly contradicts SPARK's own progress tracker on its actual card (p-015: only 2 of 4 milestones done — Proposal + Mid-term — with demo not until March 2027). Presenting an unearned, unsourced precision statistic for a project that hasn't been built/tested yet is a credibility risk if a recruiter or visitor takes the tour text at face value. Fix: correct selector to #p-015, remove or caveat the precision claim until it's real.

MEDIUM
6. achievements.html #achv-26 (Machine Learning Hackathon, WiseBee): displayed date "2 Dec 2023" but the linked asset assets/events/machine-learning-hackathon-2024.webp embeds year 2024 in its filename — one of the two is wrong; needs Aaradhya to confirm actual event date.

7. robots.txt AI-bot allowlist (GPTBot, Google-Extended, anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Applebot-Extended) — confirmed via current web sourcing that all three vendors already-listed have since split off additional tokens not present here: OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot / ChatGPT-User, Anthropic's Claude-SearchBot / Claude-User, Perplexity's Perplexity-User. README's stated "AEO Optimization" intent for this file is only partially realized against the current 2026 landscape. Fix: quarterly-review and add the missing tokens (low effort, all Allow: /).

8. sitemap.xml — every single <lastmod> across all 9 URLs is blanket-stamped 2026-08-13 regardless of which page actually changed that day (this is a sync.ps1 side-effect, not a real per-page freshness signal). Undermines the crawl-priority signal sitemap.xml exists to provide. Not caught by verify.py's check_sitemap_sync (which only checks page-existence parity, not lastmod accuracy).

LOW / NIT
9. README.md states "Instant Cross-Page Search: ... all 36 achievements, all 22 projects" (also echoed in older dev-logs/PortfolioWebsite_TRACKER.md entries) — stale vs. live DOM (37 achievements, 30 project cards / 29 unique post-dedup). Achievement count is close; project count is off by ~36%, compounding finding #2 above once that duplicate is fixed (true count becomes 29, still off from README's 22 by 7).

10. index.html JSON-LD Person.alternateName includes "Aaradhya Nepal" and "Aaradhya Engineer" — reads as SEO keyword-stuffing (name+generic-descriptor combos nobody actually calls him) rather than genuine alternate names schema.org's alternateName is meant for. Judgment call, flagging as such per task instructions rather than asserting it's wrong.

11. index.html JSON-LD WebSite.alternateName includes "ADT Games" — no games-related content, product, or context found anywhere else in the repo. Likely stray/leftover from an earlier branding exploration; worth a one-line confirmation from Aaradhya on whether to keep or drop.

12. achievements.html #achv-8: aria-label reads "Electronics For All Mentorship 2025" while the visible <h3> title says "Mentor — Electronics For All Workshop". "Workshop" vs "Mentorship" is a real wording drift between visible and accessible/assistive-tech text for the same event.

13. index.html/contact.html/about.html Person JSON-LD uses alumniOf for Kathmandu Engineering College while jobTitle/description/FAQPage still frame him as a current BEI IV/I student (graduating Jan 2027 per his own stated context). schema.org's alumniOf semantically implies completed affiliation ("alumnus of"); low-severity semantic tension — commonly used loosely in the wild for current students too, so not asserting this is wrong, just noting the mismatch.

Not independently re-verified (out of this track's file scope per task spec, flagging for whichever track/pass covers it): journey.html's own internal date/commit-SHA claims, and whether the "8 Roles & Contributions" / "2 Fellowships & Grants" stat-counter figures on index.html reconcile against experience.html — both outside the assigned file list (achievements.html, projects.html, about.html, index.html JSON-LD, sitemap.xml, robots.txt) but touched only incidentally above where they intersected a confirmed finding.
